Cache lookup/storage is applied only for `GET` and `HEAD` requests by default. Other HTTP methods bypass the cache middleware. You can change this via the `Methods` config field (for example, adding `fiber.MethodQuery`). If you supply a custom `KeyGenerator` and enable a body-bearing method such as `QUERY`, make sure it incorporates `c.Request().Body()` and those two headers, otherwise requests with the same URL but different bodies will collide. With [`StreamRequestBody`](../api/fiber.md#streamrequestbody), a request whose body is chunked or declares more than `BodyLimit` bypasses the cache (`X-Cache: unreachable`) and its body is left unread for the handler, so a key generator never reads more than `BodyLimit`.

-If a response sets `Vary`, request lookup/storage is also partitioned by those header values unless `DisableVaryHeaders` is `true`. Each response is stored under the headers its own `Vary` names, while a lookup uses the list of the response stored last for the URL: when the responses of one URL name different lists, a variant stored under another list is a miss until a response names that list again, so send the same `Vary` on every response of a URL to keep all of them reachable. Both use the header values the request carried when it reached the cache, so middleware registered after it that rewrites a request header, as `encryptcookie` does with the cookies it decrypts, does not change the key. A header such middleware adds, as one deriving `X-User-Id` from the session cookie does when the client sent none, is a dimension no request's key selects by, and so is a cookie it adds beside the ones the client sent, so a response that varies on it is not stored and is sent with `X-Cache: unreachable`. When such middleware overwrites a header the client sent, the key keeps the client's value, which the cache cannot tell from a rewrite such as the decryption: a response derived from another input, the session cookie here, must vary on that input as well (`Vary: Cookie, X-User-Id`), or the cache must be registered behind the middleware that derives it, or any client sending the header, a placeholder included, is served another client's page. A header it removes, as `encryptcookie` removes a cookie it cannot decrypt, keeps the client's key, and the response stored under it is the one for the header's absence. With `MaxBytes` set, the URL's record of that list, its Vary manifest, is deleted by the next stored response once no entry stored under it is left, so URLs evicted to stay within the limit leave none behind. Responses with `Vary: *` remain uncacheable, and so does a response whose `Vary` names more than 32 fields or is longer than 2048 bytes. That holds when `DisableVaryHeaders` is `true` as well.

Each response is stored under the headers its own `Vary` names, while a lookup uses the list of the response stored last for the URL: when the responses of one URL name different lists, a variant stored under another list is a miss until a response names that list again, so send the same `Vary` on every response of a URL to keep all of them reachable. Both use the header values the request carried when it reached the cache, and a response is stored only if the headers it varies on reach the handler as they came. Middleware registered after the cache that adds, rewrites or removes one of them, as `encryptcookie` does with the cookies it decrypts or drops, or as one deriving `X-User-Id` from the session cookie does, builds the page from a value the key does not hold: stored under the client's value, the page would be served to every client sending the same one, a placeholder included. Such a response is not stored and is sent with `X-Cache: unreachable`, and so is one that varies on a cookie such middleware adds beside the ones the client sent. Register the cache behind that middleware, so the lookup reads what the handler does, and have a response derived from another input vary on the input the client sends (`Vary: Cookie`) rather than on the header derived from it. With `MaxBytes` set, the URL's record of that list, its Vary manifest, is deleted by the next stored response once no entry stored under it is left, so URLs evicted to stay within the limit leave none behind. Responses with `Vary: *` remain uncacheable, and so does a response whose `Vary` names more than 32 fields or is longer than 2048 bytes. That holds when `DisableVaryHeaders` is `true` as well.

With an external `Storage`, an entry is decoded under size limits, and a response past one of them is not stored and reports `unreachable`: 256 bytes for `Content-Type` and `ETag`, 128 for `Content-Encoding` and `Expires`, 2048 for `Cache-Control`, and for the stored header list (`Location`, or every header with `StoreResponseHeaders`) 1024 fields with 512 bytes per name and 16384 per value. The default in-memory store keeps the entry as it is and has no such limits.
The same applies to any handler wrapper of the form

Cache hits replay the stored `Vary` header even when `StoreResponseHeaders` is off, and a hit on an entry keyed by a cookie or credential (`Vary: Cookie`, `KeyCookies`, `KeyCredentialHeaders`, or `KeyHeaders` naming `Cookie`, `Authorization` or another header that carries a credential) is sent with `Cache-Control: private` rather than `public`, so a shared cache in front of the app does not store one user's response for the next.

-A response is stored under the request headers its own `Vary` names, also when other responses of the same URL name a different list, so a page sent with `Vary: Cookie` is served only to requests with the same `Cookie`. The values are the ones the request carried when it reached the cache: middleware registered after it that rewrites a request header, as `encryptcookie` does with the cookies it decrypts, no longer changes the key a response is stored under. A response that varies on a header such middleware added, to a request that sent none, is not stored, since no request's key selects by it; a header the client sent and the middleware overwrote keeps the client's value in the key, so a response derived from another input must vary on that input too.

+A response is stored under the request headers its own `Vary` names, also when other responses of the same URL name a different list, so a page sent with `Vary: Cookie` is served only to requests with the same `Cookie`. The values are the ones the request carried when it reached the cache, and a response is stored only if the headers it varies on reach the handler as they came. A response that varies on a header middleware registered after the cache added, rewrote or removed, as `encryptcookie` does with the cookies it decrypts or drops, is not stored and is sent with `X-Cache: unreachable`: its key holds the value the client sent, which any client sending the same one, a placeholder the middleware overwrote with its session's included, would have been served the page for. Register the cache behind such middleware, and have a response derived from another input vary on the input the client sends, such as `Cookie`.

A request the server refused while reading it, such as one over `BodyLimit`, is neither served from the cache nor stored: its route never ran. With `QUERY` in `Methods`, the default key includes `Content-Type` and `Content-Encoding` besides the body. With an external `Storage`, a response past the size limits an entry is decoded under is not stored (`X-Cache: unreachable`) instead of making every later lookup of its key fail with `500`.
